page: Vultr vhf-2c-2gb is a virtual machine belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. Single-core stress-ng performance is average at 1425.29, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 24.24 GB/sec. However, multi-core stress-ng performance falls into the weak category at 2786.09, and the Passmark CPU score is 3137.23. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 18.67 GB/sec and write speeds at 12.65 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also reflect lower-tier performance.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and limited 2.0 GB memory capacity, this server is positioned for entry-level workloads rather than resource-intensive databases or large-scale applications. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic development environments, single-threaded utility scripts, and small-scale testing. The inclusion of 80 GB NVMe SSD storage provides fast local disk access relative to the compute constraints, offering a balanced storage-to-compute ratio for budget-conscious deployments.
